poolReview.rationale: Familiar everyday discrepancy has evidence-backed explanation with an honest unresolved boundary.

candidates.subject: Why your own touch usually fails to make you laugh
candidates.novelty: The same person feels external and self-touch differently.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: 1998 original comparison, 2019 robot learning experiment, 2022 attenuation/gating experiment and gargalesis experiment, 2025 review.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Understand motor-related prediction and weaker self-touch, while distinguishing light ticklishness from incompletely explained tickle laughter.
candidates.visualPotential: Coherent sculpted body and connected self-hand; prediction and feedback are an abstract model, not a brain circuit.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: Why can their fingers do what mine usually cannot?
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original procedural three-dimensional forms, deterministic animation, existing local narrator.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Everyday knowledge selected by owner; no taxonomy rule.
candidates.comparison: Owner selects the subject; investigation selects qualified framing.
limitations: Most classic self-tickle research measures light touch, not laughter.
Prediction contributes to tactile attenuation; it is not a complete proven explanation of gargalesis.

curiosityReview.honestPremise: Why your own touch usually fails to make you laugh
curiosityReview.coldAudienceReason: A lifelong familiar experience has an unexpected connection to predicting our own actions.
curiosityReview.storyRoute: External ribs and self-hand contrast → touch persists → prediction model → reduced sensation → experiment → delay evidence → light touch versus laughter → qualified payoff.

truthBoundary.rationale: Usually, can, important clue; no complete cancellation, universal incapacity or solved laughter mechanism.
